items.title: Show HN: Sigmajp – Integrated Japanese Reader
items.contentSnippet:
I always recommend yomitan and Anki to other intermediate Japanese learners, and if they try it they love it, but they only try it if I set it up for them.
I combined an epub reader with a Japanese text parser and dictionary so that tap-to-lookup a word works with no setup. Then I added flash card creation and spaced repetition reviews. And a built-in 'explain' button that asks an LLM to translate and explain the grammar for a sentence. You can also ask follow-up questions after that.
I know it'

items.title: Show HN: TickerTown, a pixel-art stock market simulator
items.contentSnippet:
Hello, HN. i'm Willis. Ian and I built TickerTown together.
Paper-trading tools out there felt super damn boring to me, so I wanted the practice to feel like play! I personally lost money "vibe investing." Only to learn there are simple strategies to learn. I hope TickerTown can help everyone by:
(a) sharing more strategies to explore,
(b) learn what type of investor you are through play,
(c) test before putting real money. avoid vibe investing,
(d) learn from others,
(e) have fun!

items.title: Show HN: OpenPetCam – a self-hosted pet camera that goes looking for your dog
items.contentSnippet:
I wanted a camera for our dog that didn't stream my living room through a vendor's cloud, and that could answer "where is she?" without me steering a joystick. OpenPetCam is what came out of that.
The camera is a cheap pan/tilt model reflashed with Thingino (open firmware). It dials out over WireGuard to a $5 VPS, so nothing is open on the home network. The server relays WebRTC to your phone, records a rolling 6 hours, and runs the detection.
